## Style Customizer

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/style-customizer/>

The Style Customizer lets you change how your form looks — colors, fonts, spacing, borders, and button style — without writing any CSS. It’s built directly into the form builder’s **Style** tab, with a live preview that updates as you make changes.

This article covers the current Style Customizer. If you styled a form before this update, don’t worry — your existing look carries over automatically the first time you open the Style tab. See **Migrating an Older Form** below.

## Where to Find It

- Go to **Everest Forms → All Forms** and edit the form you want to style.

- Click the **Style** tab at the top of the builder.

## The Style Tab Layout

The Style tab is split into two panes:

- **Left — Design controls.** A single scrollable list: **Pre-defined** (Template and Colors) at the top, then **Elements** (Form, Text, Inputs, Choices, Button, Messages) to fine-tune each part, then **Advanced** (Custom CSS) at the bottom.

- **Right — Live preview.** Shows exactly how the form will look, updating instantly as you adjust a control. Use the **Desktop / Tablet / Mobile** switch above the preview to check how your styling holds up on smaller screens.

**Note:** Nothing is saved until you click **Save** in the top-right corner. Switching to another tab (e.g. Fields) while you have unsaved style changes will ask you to confirm before leaving.

## Color Palette

At the top of the Design list, click **Colors** to open the palette screen. It has two parts:

- **Your Palette** — the six colors (background, text, borders, button, and so on) your form is actually using right now, shown as a swatch strip. On Pro, click the pencil icon to edit any of the six directly — the live preview updates as you type. On Free, this strip is view-only.

- **Presets** — a grid of ready-made color sets below it. Hover a card to preview it live on the form without committing to anything; click to apply it. Applying a preset always shows up as one step in **Undo**, so it’s safe to try a few before settling on one.

**Note (Free plan):** Two presets — **Classic** and **Monochrome** — are available on the Free plan. All other presets shown are Pro; selecting one will prompt you to upgrade. Editing Your Palette’s colors directly is also a Pro feature. See Free vs Pro below.

**If this form was styled before this update:** whatever custom palette it used to have shows up right at the front of the Presets grid, marked with a purple **Custom** badge — it isn’t hidden or lost. Click it to keep using it exactly as before. If you no longer need it, Pro plans can remove it with the delete icon on the card. What you can’t do anymore is rename it or edit its colors in place — that “create/edit a saved palette” workflow has been retired. To move it forward instead: apply it (or it may already be applied, showing as your current Your Palette), then use the **Your Palette** editor above (Pro) to adjust any of its six colors directly — you’re editing your form’s live colors at that point, not the old saved entry, so there’s nothing to “fix” beyond that.

## Design Elements

Below Pre-defined, click any of the six elements to open its settings:

### Form

Background color and image, corner rounding, overall width, and the form’s font family.

### Text

Typography (size, weight, color, style) for **Label**, **Sublabel**, **Description**, and **Section Title** text — switch between them using the tabs at the top of the panel.

### Inputs

Styling for text boxes, dropdowns, textareas, date pickers, and the file upload area, with separate **Normal** and **Focus** states.

### Choices

One shared style for every “pick a choice” field — radio buttons, checkboxes, Yes/No, image choices, star/scale ratings, Likert rows, and payment pickers (including the Subscription Plan card). Includes:

- **Selected color**, **mark size**, **unselected border**

- **Style variation** — Default, Outline, or Filled

- **Option font size**, **text color**, and **font style**

- **Alignment** — left, center, or right

### Button

Styling for the Submit button (and Multi-Part navigation/upload buttons, which follow it), with separate **Normal** and **Hover** states.

### Messages

Styling for the success, error, and validation messages shown to visitors after they submit the form. (Pro)

## Click-to-Edit in the Live Preview

Instead of hunting through the panels, click directly on any part of the form in the live preview — a label, a button, an input, a choice field — and the Design panel automatically navigates to that element’s specific settings, with the element itself outlined in the preview so you always know what you’re editing.

**Tip:** Hover over an element in the preview first; it highlights so you know exactly what you’re about to click before you commit.

## Apply Theme Style

Toggle **Apply Theme Style** (below Pre-defined) to let your active WordPress theme style the form instead of Everest Forms’ own default look. Your color, spacing, and font choices above still apply on top of either.

## Undo, Redo, and Reset

- Use the **Undo**/**Redo** buttons above the design panels to step back and forward through your recent changes.

- **Reset this section** (top of each panel) clears just that element back to its defaults.

- **Reset all styles** (top of the Design list) reverts the entire form to its unstyled default look.

## Templates

Click **Template** at the top of the Design list to browse ready-made looks and apply one in a single click. It has the same two-part layout as Colors:

- **Your Template** — a live thumbnail matching your form’s current styling exactly, right now, however you arrived at it (a preset, hand-picked colors, or a mix).

- **Presets** — the template grid below it. Hover a card to preview it live on the form; click to apply. Two presets, **Clearline** and **Ledger**, are available on the Free plan; the rest (Carbon Mono, Lavendar, Scribble, Lines, Sage Card, Editorial, Midnight Rain) are Pro.

**Note:** Applying a template replaces your current colors, fonts, and spacing with the template’s own — it’s a starting point you can still fine-tune afterward.

**If this form was styled before this update:** any custom template you’d saved for it shows up first in the Presets grid, marked **Custom** — same treatment as a custom palette (see above). Click it to reapply, or Pro plans can delete it with the card’s delete icon. It can no longer be renamed or edited as a saved entry — to build on it, apply it and then adjust the result with the Design Elements panels (Form, Text, Inputs, Choices, Button, Messages) below; those changes apply to your form directly and show up live in Your Template above.

## Custom CSS

Click **Custom CSS** under Advanced to write your own CSS. This is applied site-wide — the same Additional CSS used across every form on your site, not just this one — so a rule you add here will show up wherever it applies, on any form.

On the Free plan, styling a form means picking one of the two built-in palette or template presets (and/or writing Custom CSS) — the granular design panels are visible so you can see what’s possible, but are locked until you upgrade.

## Migrating an Older Form

If a form was styled using the classic (older) Style Customizer, opening its Style tab for the first time automatically converts that styling to the current format — nothing is lost, including any Pro styling if your Pro license has since lapsed and later comes back.

## Email Templates

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/email-template/>

The Everest Forms **Email Templates** Add-on allows you to create different email templates that you can use to send emails to your users. The templates can be created from scratch or you can simply get started with the available templates. You can customize the templates completely as per your requirement.

## Installation

- Firstly, you need to purchase the Everest Forms Pro plugin.
- After the successful purchase, you will get the plugin zip file under your WPEverest account page.
- Now, you can download the **Everest Forms Pro** plugin and **Email Templates** addon from there.
- Through your WordPress Dashboard, visit **Plugins -> Add New -> Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip file and then install and activate it.
- Now you are ready to use this add-on for your site.

## Creating an Email Template

Once you have completed the above tasks of installing and activating the plugin and add-on, You can move on to creating the templates.
Go to the **Everest Forms -> Email Templates** from your Dashboard and then click on **Add New**. Here, you can either create an entirely new template or get started with an existing template.

You will then be shown a page(see below) where either you can select from existing pre-made Email templates or Start from Scratch. However, in both cases, you can customize them as per your needs.

Click on the Email Template that you want to use, give it a name and then the next step will be to Customize the Selected Email Template.

## Customizing the Email Template

After you have selected the Email Template, you can customize almost every part of the template with the Customizing options.

You will see the customizing options on your left. I will briefly tell you about every available option.

**1. General:** The general option will let you customize the typography and color of the selected email template. You can choose between different fonts, adjust the font size and line-height for different headings and the body text. And in the Colors option, you can choose different colors for different headings and body text.

**2. Container:** The container option will let you customize both the Inside and Outside area of the email template container. You can add a background color to your email template and adjust the spacing. It will also let you add a background image or color to the email template.

**3. Header:** The Header option will allow you to play with three things of the header part of email template. You can customize the logo, the header content, and the Layout/Styling of the logo and content.

**4. Body:** The Body option will allow you to customize the body section of the email template. You can customize 3 different aspect of the body section which is, typography, colors and styles. You can set particular background colors and select a different font size for the body text.

**5. Footer:** The footer option will let you customize the footer part of the email template. You can customize the Primary Footer of the template and also add a Footer Copyright text and then customize it.

**6. Additional CSS:** As the name suggests itself, Additional CSS can be used to to add your own CSS codes to customize the way you want.

## Using the Email Template

Finally, after selecting the template and customizing it, the template is ready to use, and it’s straightforward to use it. For this, go to your Contact Form Email Settings , and Scroll to the bottom of it and you will find the option to choose the template.

Choose the email template that you made. Save the changes and that’s all. The received email will be wrapped in the email template that you selected.
